newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish ailing brewery Lezajsk to fire 200 workers.
newsitem.headline: Polish ailing brewery Lezajsk to fire 200 workers.

text.p: Polish brewery Lezajsk SA, whose sell-off has been delayed for years, plans to dismiss 200 of its 950 workers due to deteriorating economic situation, PAP news agency said on Wednesday.

It quoted Lezajsk President Wieslaw Walczyk as saying that the lay-offs, to be carried out by February next year, result from declining sales caused by the lack of proper marketing and low work efficiency.
Lezajsk's financial situation has declined because unlike Poland's other major breweries it has not been privatised, Walczyk was quoted as saying.
The brewery's trade unions are protesting against the planned lay-offs.

Privatisation Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said last month that the sale of Lezajsk, which was earmarked for privatisation in 1993, was likely to be further delayed as two of the three shortlisted bidders withdrew from negotiations.
The government is offering up to 75 percent of Lezajsk, in southeastern Poland, while 20 percent is earmarked for employees and five percent for reprivatisation claims.
Lezajsk had a 90,000-zloty net profit in 1994 against 71.7 million zlotys in sales. The ministry has not published data for 1995 and 1996.
